summary.intent: Finish rolling out a CI change that adds a single required `firmware-gate` check, replacing the three per-shard firmware test checks. This means verifying the gate on Depot for both the 'due and passed' and 'not due, skipped' paths, and updating the branch protection ruleset to match.
summary.outcome: The first CI run was green and the gate's 'due and passed' path was confirmed. The follow-up commit c0e4492 (smarter uv.lock check, --no-renames, five pins) was pushed and the four trail #278 findings resolved. The user updated the ruleset, which was read back and confirmed to require lint, pre-commit, tools-tests and firmware-gate. A throwaway docs-only draft PR was then opened (docs/ci-skip-check.md) to exercise the skip path, but its result isn't known yet.

repo: CI workflow (`CI`) has a `changes` job that outputs `firmware=true/false`, three `firmware-tests` shards, and a `firmware-gate` job that logs `changes=... firmware_due=... tests=...` and passes when tests succeed or are legitimately skipped.
Firmware shards take about 4 to 14 minutes each (observed 12m18s, 13m40s, 4m1s), so a full CI run on firmware-touching changes takes roughly 14 minutes.
Edits to `tools/` or `pyproject.toml` trigger `firmware=true`, so those changes always run the shards.

Required checks on main are now `CI / lint`, `CI / pre-commit`, `CI / tools-tests` and `CI / firmware-gate`. The per-shard `firmware-tests (...)` checks were removed from the ruleset so that a skipped shard doesn't block merging.
The skip path should be verified by a Renovate PR that only moves ruff, ty or pytest, or by a docs-only PR.
workflow: The `gh` CLI reads `GH_TOKEN` from the environment by default. Unsetting it makes `gh` fall back to the user's keychain token, which has admin permissions (needed to read repo rulesets).
A required status check only appears in the branch protection picker after it has run at least once, so the gate had to run before the ruleset could be switched.
Use normal pushes (no force) for follow-up commits, and read rulesets read-only unless asked to change them.
A throwaway docs-only draft PR is a cheap way to exercise a CI skip path before relying on it for merges.

friction: The admin token was not available by default: `GH_TOKEN` in the environment lacked ruleset admin permissions, so the user had to explain how to fall back to the keychain token.
Each CI verification cycle costs around 14 minutes of waiting on the firmware shards.
open_items: Confirm the docs-only PR shows `firmware=false`, skipped shards, and `firmware-gate` logging `tests=skipped` and passing.
Check that the run on c0e4492 finishes with `firmware-gate` passing on the new uv.lock-aware script.
Close and delete the throwaway docs-only PR and branch (docs/ci-skip-check.md) once the skip path is verified.
Watch the first Renovate PR that moves only ruff, ty or pytest after merge, as a real-world check of the skip path.
